questions.question: Which among the following is a database software?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dBase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• What is a Database?

 
 
• A database is a collection of related data which represents some aspect of the real world. A database system is designed to be built and populated with data for a certain task.
 
 
 
• What is DBMS?
 
 
• Database Management System (DBMS) is a software for storing and retrieving users' data while considering appropriate security measures. It consists of a group of programs that manipulate the database. The DBMS accepts the request for data from an application and instructs the operating system to provide the specific data. In large systems, a DBMS helps users and other third-party software to store and retrieve data.
 
• DBMS allows users to create their own databases as per their requirements. The term “DBMS” includes the use of the database and other application programs. It provides an interface between the data and the software application.
 
• Some DBMS examples include MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft Access, SQL Server, FileMaker, Oracle, RDBMS, dBASE, Clipper, and FoxPro. Since there are so many database management systems available, it is important for there to be a way for them to communicate with each other. For this reason, most database software comes with an Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver that allows the database to integrate with other databases. For example, common SQL statements such as SELECT and INSERT are translated from a program's proprietary syntax into a syntax other databases can understand.
 
 

 
• **dBase **is considered to be the 1st DBMS software for all types of microcomputer systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct full form of VOIP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Voice over Internet Protocol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP)** is a technology that allows you to make voice calls using a broadband Internet connection instead of a regular (or analog) phone line.
 
• VoIP converts your voice into a digital signal that travels over the Internet. If you are calling a regular phone number, the signal is converted to a regular telephone signal before it reaches the destination.
 
• VoIP services can be used with a VoIP phone, a traditional phone with a VoIP adapter, or a computer with VoIP software.
 
• VoIP is advantageous because it can offer lower costs, especially for long-distance or international calls, and can integrate with other services available over the Internet, such as video calls, messaging, or data sharing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **VoIP Protocols**

 
 
• VoIP uses various protocols to facilitate communication over the internet, including **SIP (Session Initiation Protocol)**, **H.323**, and **RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol)**.
 
• SIP is widely used for signaling and controlling multimedia communication sessions.
 
• RTP is used for delivering audio and video over IP networks.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of VoIP**
 
 
• Cost Savings: VoIP calls, especially international ones, are generally cheaper than traditional phone calls.
 
• Flexibility: VoIP can be used on various devices, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, and desktop computers.
 
• Integration: VoIP services can be integrated with other internet services, such as email, web browsing, and instant messaging.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of VoIP**
 
 
• Reliability: VoIP services depend on a stable internet connection. Any disruptions in internet service can affect call quality or cause dropped calls.
 
• Emergency Calls: VoIP services may not provide reliable location information for emergency services, which is a significant concern in case of emergencies.
 
• Security: VoIP communications are susceptible to hacking, eavesdropping, and other security breaches if not properly secured.

questions.question: What is the full form of NetBIOS?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NetBIOS, an acronym for Network Basic Input/Output System, is a suite of protocols that enables applications on different computers within a local area network (LAN) to communicate with each other.
 
• Developed in the 1980s, NetBIOS primarily serves as an application programming interface (API), providing a set of functions that applications can use to access network services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Name Resolution: NetBIOS allows applications to locate other devices on the network using unique names instead of complex network addresses.
 
• This simplifies communication between devices.
 
• **Session Management: **NetBIOS facilitates the establishment, maintenance, and termination of communication sessions between devices. A session provides a reliable channel for data exchange between applications.
 
• **Data Exchange:** Once a session is established, NetBIOS enables applications to exchange data with other applications on the network. This data can include files, messages, and other types of information.
 
• While NetBIOS was originally developed for use on IBM PC networks, it has since been adapted to work with various operating systems and network technologies. It is particularly well-suited for smaller networks where simplicity and ease of use are paramount.
 
• However, NetBIOS has certain limitations, such as its lack of support for large-scale networks and its reliance on older protocols. As a result, newer technologies like TCP/IP and DNS have largely superseded NetBIOS in modern networking environments.
 
• Despite its limitations, NetBIOS remains relevant in some legacy systems and niche applications. It continues to provide a basic framework for communication within small, localized networks, especially where compatibility with older systems is a concern.

questions.question: What is used for holding program instructions that can't be changed throughout the life of the computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ROM**

 
 
• Read-Only Memory is a ROM in a computer.
 
• Read-only memory is a storage medium that permanently stores data on computers and electronic devices.
 
• The data stored in these chips is nonvolatile i.e. it is not lost when power is removed.
 
• There are five basic ROM types:
 
 
• ROM: Read-Only Memory.
 
• PROM: Programmable read-only memory.
 
• EPROM: Erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• EEPROM: Electrically erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• Flash memory: Flash memory, a type of EEPROM that uses in-circuit wiring. 
 
 
 
• BIOS uses Flash memory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Register**

 
 
• The smallest and fastest memory of a computer is registered memory located in the computer's central processing unit(CPU).
 
• It generally stores the most used instructions, data, etc. which are to be used by CPU.
 
• Control Unit is part of the CPU.
 
• It advises the input and output devices, and computer memory on how to respond to the instructions sent to the processor.
 
 
 
• **RAM**
 
 
• It stores data that the computer needs to use temporarily. So it is faster than the secondary storage devices. It is a volatile memory i.e. the data disappear from it when the power is off.
 
• It is known as the Read-Write Memory. i.e. the user can write information into RAM and read information from it.
 
• It is called random access since any memory location can be accessed randomly for reading and writing. The access time is the same for each memory location.
 
• It is usually called “temporary” memory, which means that when the system is shut down, the memory is lost.
 
 
 
• **Cache**
 
 
• A cache memory is used by the central processing unit of a computer to reduce the average cost time or energy to access data from the** main memory**. 
 
• Generally Cache memory is logically positioned between** CPU** and **main memory**.

questions.question: Neel wants to use a Character Printer. Which among the following should he pick?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dot Matrix Printer.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Printer is an **output device**.
 
• Dot matrix printers, also known as pin printers, are the most popular type of **impact printer.**
 
• These printers have a matrix of pins on their print heads to create **characters or graphics.** 
 
• Dot-matrix printers usually have **9 to 24 pins** in the print head.
 
• Dot-matrix printers are **cheap **and usually print 100–600 characters per second. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drum Printer-**

 
 
• Drum printer is a type of **impact printer**.
 
• The drum printer consists of a rotating cylindrical drum with a circular band of characters on its surface.
 
• In particular, the surface is divided into tracks equal to the size of the supported printing paper.
 
• Drum Printer printing speed is quite fast ( 300 - 2,000 lines per minute), they make a lot of noise. 
 
 
 
• **Laser Printer-**
 
 
• Laser printers are **non-impact printers,** typically using laser or non-impact photocopier technology to produce the dots needed to print text or images on paper.
 
• Laser printers can produce extremely high-resolution prints.
 
• This can vary from 300 dpi (Dots Per Inch) to 1200 dpi depending on system capacity and memory availability. 
 
 
 
• **Chain Printer-**
 
 
• Chain printer is a type of **impact printer**.
 
• The chain printer consists of a revolving chain with characters set on its surface. These printers typically have a character set of **48, 64, or 96 characters.**
 
• Chain printer can print 300 - 500 **lines of characters per minute.**

questions.question: IBM 360 was developed in which of the following generations of computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Third Generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The IBM System/360 **was announced and developed in the** mid-1965s, during the period associated with third-generation computers.**
 
• Third-generation computers were defined by the use of **integrated circuits (ICs) or semiconductor chips, which represented a significant advancement over the previous generation's technology.**
 
• The** System/360** was a groundbreaking series of** compatible mainframe computers, allowing customers to upgrade from lower-cost models to larger systems without having to rewrite their applications.**
 
• It also introduced the** 8-bit byte to the commercial world, which remains a fundamental data management unit today.**
 
• **The S/360** was not just a computer but a whole series of computers that helped to establish the concept of a computer **"family".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation:**

 
 
• These computers** (late 1946s to mid-1959s) were based on vacuum tubes.**
 
• They were large, expensive, and generated a lot of heat.
 
• Examples include the **ENIAC and UNIVAC.**
 
 
 
• **Second Generation:**
 
 
• Second generation computers** (mid-1959s to mid-1965s) moved from vacuum tubes to transistors, which were smaller, faster, cheaper, and more reliable.**
 
• **IBM's 7000 series belongs to this generation.**
 
 
 
• **Fourth Generation:**
 
 
• These computers** (1971 to the mid-1980s) are characterized by microprocessors which contain many, sometimes millions, of ICs.**
 
• **Personal computers, such as the IBM PC, fall into this category.**
